CSE - Parse Script.vi

Owning Palette: CSE Script Processor

The VI parses a CSE script and returns a reference to a CSE instance context containing the parsed script. This reference is to be used to execute a script with CSE - Execute Parsed Script.vi. In addition, the VI loads FuncVIs required to execute a script.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

directives defines parsing directives:
enaNamedConst enables (TRUE) or disables (FALSE) treating Named Constants during script parsing. This behavior can be altered during the parsing phase by using the $NCON (enable) and $NCOFF (disable) Parsing Directives directly within the script.
Script name is an optional parameter. If you specify a script name, it will appear in an error message along with a line number in order to indicate location of both parsing and runtime errors.
Script is to be parsed. See CSE Script Syntax for details.
load FuncVIs specifies a method to load FuncVIs. Make the VI to load FuncVIs if a script can contain calls of FuncVI functions; it has two advantages. First, CSE can detect an invalid function call while parsing but not evaluating. Second, CSE will be able to evaluate a script much faster if all required FuncVIs are preliminary loaded.

0don't loadThe VI doesn't load FuncVIs.
1loadThe VI loads FuncVIs of the functions that are not recognized as embedded (FastFunc) functions.
2load & testThe VI loads FuncVIs as described above. In addition, the VI verifies calls of FuncVI functions for correct number of parameters. The VI returns an error if any mismatch found. This is default value.
action specifies an operation to perform:

0parseThe VI parses Script and stores its parsed version (the parsed script) in a static context of the current VI instance. This is default value.
1parse (dyn instance)The VI creates a dynamic instance context and stores the parsed script in it; the static context stays unchanged. This way, a single instance of the VI can produce more than one parsed script.
2test syntaxThe VI parses Script and stores the parsed script in the static context. The VI unloads FuncVIs after completion if it has loaded any according to load FuncVI specifier.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
parameters specifies optional parameters:
AutoParse. If FALSE, the VI parses the script every time it is called. If TRUE (default), the VI bypasses the parsing phase if the static context of the called VI instance already contains a compiled version of the input script. This optimization significantly decreases the aggregate time required to parse and execute a script when called inside a loop. Note that the VI always parses the script when creating a dynamic instance context.
GroupStm. If TRUE, the VI groups sequential expression statements into a single statement. This optimization can increase script execution speed. The default value is FALSE.
ErrSrcMaxLen defines the maximum length of a quotation from a source script in error messages. The default value is 180.
CSE RefNum returns a reference number of CSE instance context containing the parsed script. If you specify action control equal to 1 (parse (dyn instance)), CSE RefNum returns a reference to a new-created dynamic instance context. Otherwise, it contains a reference to the static context of the called VI instance. Note that a dynamic context should be explicitly closed even if the VI returns an error.
loaded functions returns function names whose FuncVIs have been loaded at the current call of the VI. Note that VI only loads FuncVIs that are not loaded yet (more precise, FuncVIs to which CalcExpress doesn't have opened VI Reference).
dynamic instance returns TRUE if a dynamic CSE instance context has been created to store the parsed script. The VI creates dynamic context if action is equal to 1 (parse (dyn instance)).
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
parsed returns TRUE if an input script was actually parsed. Otherwise, it returns FALSE that means the static context of the called VI instance already contains a parsed version of the input script.

 

CSE - Parse Script.vi - details

The VI is reentrant, each instance of it has its own context to store a script parsed last (called a static context). In addition, you can make the VI create a dynamic instance context if a single VI instance should produce a few parsed scripts; e.g. within a loop. Note that each dynamic context is unique in difference from the static context. A dynamic context should be explicitly closed with the help of CSE - Close Instance.vi. Furthermore, all opened dynamic contexts will be implicitly closed when this VI is unloaded; i.e. no its instances stay in memory.
